What he sort of said but didn't articulate well is the situation of SAP. SAP is not on a normal classified system. It's not about taking items from a classified system to a private system. This is about going into a guarded room that is physically and electronically isolated from the standard intellegence systems and viewing documents that are very rarely digitized and physically taking it or duplicating it electronically to send to a system outside of the government.

The way it is supposed to work is you go in with a notebook and take notes on the material and the document itself never touches the classified work computers. Then that data is used to inform your writing which you base on other documents. A great deal of it is sourced from other countries that volunteer intel to us so it might be digital when they send it but it gets printed and filed never to touch any computer again, much less Hillary's household server.

Clearence to see a SAP is personally granted too. You can't just walk in and see whatever you want. The president doesn't have willy nilly access to SAP. The whole point is to make it unavailable to the intel community but still there if you need it. If CIA agents can't know this stuff then neither should Hillary and she shouldn't be carrying it around on her blackberry.

The reason these people will never go into detail is the government doesn't want people knowing that it has data that itself doesn't know.. at the highest level. It has flaws and abuse. I'm aware of at least on situation where a high level person, who's name you all know, put something into a SAP that didn't need to be in it just to keep it from another high level person, who's name you all know... to protect one of our international friends.

Edit: For clarity, why would someone want to keep data out of the hands of the intel community as a whole? Because if you know what data someone has it can lead to finding sources and if there is even one spy in the agency it would be pretty easy to piece together.
